ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A = 90^\circ$, $AD \perp BC$ at point D. If $BD = 3$ and $CD = 2$, then what is the value of $\tan B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, $AD\perp BC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAC=\angle ADC=\angle ADB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B+\angle BAD=\angle BAD+\angle CAD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B=\angle CAD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ADB\sim \triangle CAD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AD}{CD}=\frac{BD}{AD}$,\\
$\therefore$ $AD^2=BD\cdot CD$,\\
$\because$ $BD=3$, $CD=2$,\\
$\therefore$ $AD=\sqrt{6}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\tan B=\frac{AD}{BD}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows triangle ABC with A at the top, B on the left end of the horizontal base, and C on the right end of the base. Point D lies on segment BC between B and C, and segment AD is drawn from A down to D, perpendicular to BC, splitting BC into BD and DC. Reasoning: From the text, angle A = 90° and AD ⟂ BC, so angles ADB and ADC are right angles. Since triangle ABC is right at A, angles B and C are complementary. In right triangle ADC, angles CAD and C are also complementary, so angle B = angle CAD. Therefore triangles ABD and ADC are similar. From the similarity, AD/CD = BD/AD, so AD^2 = BD · CD. With BD = 3 and CD = 2, AD^2 = 6, hence AD = sqrt(6). In right triangle ABD, for angle B, the opposite side is AD and the adjacent side is BD. Thus tan B = AD/BD = sqrt(6)/3.
